title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: premises need times-distinction; positive law may be temporary
pass_a_gloss: Though he admits the syllogism's conclusion, the premises are not so clear they need no useful distinction. How does the opponent understand that the Lord gave that law not only to Adam but to all posterity, and that by it eating that fruit was forbidden to men? Times must be distinguished. If Adam had begotten children in paradise, that interdict would have bound them after they were born—unless God at last abrogated it; who knows the Lord's mind? It was positive law fencing Adam's free choice about a thing indifferent by nature, and so could be prescribed for a time and abrogated when that time elapsed, like the food-choice laws God once gave his people. Who of us can know whether God meant that ban to stand forever, or only for a certain time after which, obedience amply proved, he would have lifted it and given man free use of that tree thereafter? It does not become us to break into God's secrets or confidently assert what we do not know.
pass_b_english: Although I admit the conclusion of this syllogism of yours, yet the premises are not so clear that they do not need some distinction useful to the matter we are treating. For how, I ask, do you understand these propositions—that the Lord gave that law not only to Adam but also to all posterity; that by that law eating of that fruit was forbidden to men? Times certainly must be distinguished. For if Adam had begotten children in paradise, that interdict would have bound them after they had been born—unless perhaps God at last abrogated that interdict; for who knows the mind of the Lord? It was a positive law, fencing Adam's freedom of choice about a thing indifferent by its own nature, and so could be prescribed for a time and, that time elapsed, abrogated, just as the laws about choice of foods which God once laid down for his people. Who of us can know whether God had willed that interdict to be in force forever, or only for some certain time, which being finished, and man's obedience amply proved, he would have taken away, man being given freedom thereafter to use that tree? For it does not become us to break into God's secrets, or confidently to assert what we do not know.
source_text: Quamvis autem conclusionem huius tui syllogismi admittam, tamen non sunt ita liquida praemissae, quin aliqua distinctione egeant, ad rem quam agimus, utili. Nam quomodo, quaeso, intelligis has propositiones, Dominum legem illam dedisse non tantum Adamo, sed etiam posteris omnibus; lege illa interdictum fuisse hominibus esum illius fructus? Distinguenda certe sunt tempora. Nam si Adamus in paradiso liberos genuissent, eos, postea quam geniti fuissent, interdictum illud obligasset; nisi forte interdictum illud Deus tandem abrogasset; quis enim novit mentem Domini? Positiva lex fuit, libertatem arbitrii Adami circa rem natura sua indifferentem circumscribens, ac proinde potuit ad tempus praescribi, eoque tempore elapso abrogari, quemadmodum leges de ciborum delectu, quas Deus olim tulerat populo suo. Quis nostrum scire potest, utrum Deus voluisset interdictum illud perpetuo vigere, an vero ad certum quoddam tempus duntaxat, quo exacto, & probata abunde hominis obedientia, illud sustulisset, facta homini copia utendi in posterum illa arbore? Haud enim decet nos in Dei arcana irrumpere, aut ea quae ignoramus confidenter asseverare.

choices.choice: Premises need times-split; positive law may be temporary
